official_sources.title: LIDAR Composite DTM 1m coverage and lineage
official_sources.finding: The official 1 m DTM covers about 99% of England, is built from time-stamped and National LIDAR Programme surveys, prefers the newest best-resolution survey, and uses bilinear interpolation where resampling is required.
official_sources.limitation: Composite mosaicking can mix survey dates and resolutions; use the survey index and prefer a matching time-stamped tile for target sampling.

official_sources.title: LIDAR Composite DSM 1m surface-object contamination
official_sources.finding: The official 1 m DSM includes vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as terrain, so it cannot be substituted for a ground-only DTM when computing parcel terrain height difference.
official_sources.limitation: DSM is retained only for contamination diagnostics and surface-height comparisons.

official_sources.title: Environment Agency absolute and relative LiDAR height error
official_sources.finding: The capture specification requires absolute height error below ±15 cm RMSE and expects relative random height error no greater than ±5 cm.
official_sources.limitation: These programme specifications do not include parcel-boundary, interpolation, epoch or edge-support uncertainty.

official_sources.title: Environment Agency LiDAR point-density semantics
official_sources.finding: A 1 m DSM survey targets at least 1 point per square metre, while DTM density under vegetation can be lower; the point cloud is irregular and density must not be treated as a regular-grid resolution guarantee.
official_sources.limitation: Point-density evidence is not a direct accuracy score and must be combined with raster metadata and interior-cell support.

official_sources.title: Time-stamped DTM survey-specific transform and geoid metadata
official_sources.finding: Time-stamped DTM tiles are supplied in metres on the OS Grid and referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn; the metadata catalogue records survey date, resolution, transformation and geoidal model, which must be matched before sampling.
official_sources.limitation: The correct survey tile still requires exact spatial coverage, checksum, NoData and timestamp validation.

official_sources.title: National LIDAR Programme phase and repeat-survey coverage
official_sources.finding: The programme divided England into 302 phase-1 survey blocks captured from 2017 to 2023 and later repeats selected blocks using incrementing phase numbers; coverage metadata is available in GeoJSON, GeoPackage, shapefile and geodatabase formats.
official_sources.limitation: A later phase is not automatically best unless its product type, resolution, transform, geoid and target coverage all match.

official_sources.title: Copernicus DEM orthometric versus ellipsoidal output control
official_sources.finding: Copernicus DEM values are orthometric by default; enabling the EGM option adds EGM2008 geoid heights and returns WGS84 ellipsoidal heights. Upsampling and downsampling can use nearest, bilinear or bicubic interpolation.
official_sources.limitation: Copernicus DEM is a coarse diagnostic only and must not be mixed numerically with ODN heights without an explicit datum transformation.

official_sources.title: Copernicus GLO-30 availability and GLO-90 infill semantics
official_sources.finding: The COPERNICUS_30 service uses public GLO-30 where available and GLO-90 where 30 m tiles have not been released, so nominal 30 m requests can contain 90 m source areas.
official_sources.limitation: This mixed-resolution global DEM is not parcel-grade and is used only for broad plausibility checks.
